newsitem.title: UK: Britons back monarchy in TV poll.
newsitem.headline: Britons back monarchy in TV poll.

text.p: Britain's beleaguered royal family has been given a boost by a television viewers' poll which produced a two-to-one majority in favour of the monarchy.
Of nearly 2.5 million phone calls recorded during Tuesday night's live television debate on the monarchy, 66 percent were in favour of a future for the royal family while 34 percent were against.
The poll, which showed England, Wales and Northern Irleand backed the monarchy but Scotland did not, was carried out during a rowdy studio debate attended by more than 3,000 people.
Despite the poll result, the studio debate caused anger among royalists who felt they were frozen out of the discussion in favour of republican sympathisers and that the level of debate was low.

"Palace fury at "rigged' TV poll," declared a banner headline in the Mirror tabloid, which quoted courtiers as saying leading royalists invited onto the programme had been "dumped" so republicans could make the running.

Former Conservative government minister Steven Norris walked out of the studio debate, saying it was "trivial and patronising". Sir Bernard Ingham, former press secretary to ex-prime minister Margaret Thatcher, said the debate was a "disgrace".
Following the programme, bookmakers William Hill quoted odds of 50-1 that the monarchy would be abolished within 10 years and 25-1 that it would go within 20 years.

Support for the royal family came despite a series of scandals that have reduced its standing in recent years. Heir-to-the-throne Prince Charles and Princess Diana divorced last year after both admitted adultery.

Charles returned to London on Tuesday after a skiing holiday during which he was reported to have admitted failing the British monarchy and to have vowed to "sort the whole bloody mess out" by reaching out more to ordinary people.
His public standing was hit by the acrimonious break-up of his marriage and his confession of an extra-marital affair with long-time flame Camilla Parker Bowles.
